page.overview:
Who is Dead Men of Dunharrow?

The Dead Men of Dunharrow, known originally as the Men of the Mountains, were Men of the White Mountains cursed to remain in Middle-earth by Isildur, after they abandoned their oath to aid him in the War of the Last Alliance. They haunted the caverns beneath the Dwimorberg, and the valley of Harrowdale that lay in its shadow, though they were said to appear in the valley only in times of trouble or death. They were led by the King of the Dead. Since the line of Isildur was thought in the late Third Age to have ended, no one could call upon these Dead Men for aid, as they would only answer to the Isildurioni.

The Dead Men of Dunharrow were descended from the second host of the Edain that reached the White Mountains along with the Drúedain. Thus, they were close relatives of the House of Haleth that lived in Beleriand while they themselves stayed in the eastern regions of Middle-earth that would be later settled by the Númenóreans.

The Men of the Mountains were scattered communities of forest-dwellers without central leadership. They lived in the White Mountains during the Second Age and spoke a pre-Númenórean language that was related to Dunlendish and the Halethian language. They had worshipped Sauron in the Dark Years before the foundation of Gondor.

When Gondor was founded, they swore an oath to Isildur that they would fight for him. However, during the dark years, they had worshiped Sauron, and so when the time came and Isildur asked for their aid, they refused. And so Isildur cursed them, saying: "Thou shalt be the last king, and if the west prove mightier than thy Black Master, this curse I lay upon thee and thy folk; to rest never until your oath is fulfilled. For this war will last through years uncounted, and you shall be summoned once again ere the end." Therefore, they fled from the wrath of Isildur and dared not go forth to war for Sauron, and they hid in secret places in the mountains and had no dealings with other men. They slowly started to dwindle and the terror of the Sleepless Dead came about to all the places where they lingered.
